shortcuts.title: Open Spotlight
shortcuts.summary: Search for apps, files, and more with Spotlight.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Check that Spotlight still uses the default shortcut in System Settings.
steps: Check that Spotlight still uses the default shortcut in System Settings.
Press Command + Space.
The Spotlight search field appears. Press Esc to dismiss it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The Spotlight search field appears. Press Esc to dismiss it.
notes: Input sources or custom settings may use the same shortcut. Check the Spotlight binding in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts.

shortcuts.title: Switch apps
shortcuts.summary: Switch between running apps.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Open at least two apps.
steps: Open at least two apps.
Hold Command and press Tab to choose another app, then release Command.
The app switcher appears. Release Command to switch to the selected app.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The app switcher appears. Release Command to switch to the selected app.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Switch windows in an app
shortcuts.summary: Cycle through windows in the current app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Bring an app with at least two windows to the front.
steps: Bring an app with at least two windows to the front.
Press Command + `.
Focus moves to another window in the same app.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Focus moves to another window in the same app.
notes: The grave-accent key is usually above Tab. Other languages and keyboard layouts may use a different key; check the Window menu.

shortcuts.title: Capture the entire screen
shortcuts.summary: Take a screenshot of the whole screen.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Arrange the screen first. Screenshots use your current save location.
steps: Arrange the screen first. Screenshots use your current save location.
Press Shift + Command + 3.
A screenshot thumbnail appears in a corner, followed by the saved image.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A screenshot thumbnail appears in a corner, followed by the saved image.
notes: Screenshots save to the Desktop by default. Change the location in Screenshot → Options. Capture shortcuts can also be changed in System Settings.

shortcuts.title: Capture a selected area
shortcuts.summary: Drag to capture part of the screen.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Prepare the content you want to capture. Press Esc to cancel.
steps: Prepare the content you want to capture. Press Esc to cancel.
Press Shift + Command + 4, then drag to select an area and release.
The pointer becomes a crosshair. Drag and release to capture the area.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The pointer becomes a crosshair. Drag and release to capture the area.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Open Screenshot tools
shortcuts.summary: Choose a capture area, recording mode, and save location.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Prepare your screen. You can inspect the toolbar without starting a recording.
steps: Prepare your screen. You can inspect the toolbar without starting a recording.
Press Shift + Command + 5.
The Screenshot toolbar appears near the bottom of the screen. Press Esc to close it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The Screenshot toolbar appears near the bottom of the screen. Press Esc to close it.
notes: Start a screen recording yourself from the toolbar. QuickKey does not press the Record button for you.

shortcuts.title: Lock the screen
shortcuts.summary: Lock your Mac while keeping your session open.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Make sure you can unlock your Mac with your password or Touch ID.
steps: Make sure you can unlock your Mac with your password or Touch ID.
Press Control + Command + Q.
The lock screen appears. Unlock to return to your windows.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The lock screen appears. Unlock to return to your windows.
notes: This temporarily leaves QuickKey. Unlock with your account password or Touch ID to continue.

shortcuts.title: Open Mission Control
shortcuts.summary: See windows and desktop spaces at a glance.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Open a few windows and check the Mission Control shortcut in System Settings.
steps: Open a few windows and check the Mission Control shortcut in System Settings.
Press Control + Up Arrow.
Windows spread out. Click a window or press Esc to return.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Windows spread out. Click a window or press Esc to return.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Show an app's windows
shortcuts.summary: See all open windows in the current app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Bring an app with multiple windows to the front.
steps: Bring an app with multiple windows to the front.
Press Control + Down Arrow.
The app's windows are displayed together. Click one to select it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The app's windows are displayed together. Click one to select it.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.
aliases: 显示当前应用的所有窗口

shortcuts.title: Show or hide the Dock
shortcuts.summary: Toggle automatic hiding of the Dock.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Note whether the Dock is currently always visible.
steps: Note whether the Dock is currently always visible.
Press Option + Command + D.
Dock visibility changes. Press the shortcut again to switch back.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Dock visibility changes. Press the shortcut again to switch back.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Enter or exit full screen
shortcuts.summary: Toggle full screen in apps that support it.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Bring a window that supports full screen to the front.
steps: Bring a window that supports full screen to the front.
Press Control + Command + F.
The window enters full screen. Press the shortcut again to exit.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The window enters full screen. Press the shortcut again to exit.
notes: Not all windows support full screen. You can also move the pointer to the top and use the green window button to exit.

shortcuts.title: Open Emoji & Symbols
shortcuts.summary: Open the Character Viewer to insert emoji or symbols.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click an editable text field so the insertion point is visible.
steps: Click an editable text field so the insertion point is visible.
Press Control + Command + Space.
The character panel appears. Choosing a character inserts it into the text field.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The character panel appears. Choosing a character inserts it into the text field.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Previous input source
shortcuts.summary: Switch between enabled input sources.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Enable at least two input sources and check their shortcuts in System Settings.
steps: Enable at least two input sources and check their shortcuts in System Settings.
Press Control + Space.
The input source indicator changes. New text uses the selected input source.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The input source indicator changes. New text uses the selected input source.
notes: This requires multiple input sources and the default bindings. Input-method software may override the shortcut.

shortcuts.title: Next input source
shortcuts.summary: Select the next enabled input source.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Enable multiple input sources and check their system shortcuts.
steps: Enable multiple input sources and check their system shortcuts.
Press Control + Option + Space.
The input source indicator switches to the next available source.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The input source indicator switches to the next available source.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Copy text
shortcuts.summary: Copy the selected text to the clipboard, keeping the original.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Select some text in the practice field.
steps: Select some text in the practice field.
Press Command + C.
Pasting into the target field produces the same text as your selection.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Pasting into the target field produces the same text as your selection.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Paste text
shortcuts.summary: Insert clipboard text at the current position.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Copy some practice text, then click the paste target field.
steps: Copy some practice text, then click the paste target field.
Press Command + V.
The clipboard text appears in the target field.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The clipboard text appears in the target field.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Cut text
shortcuts.summary: Move the selected text to the clipboard.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Select text in the practice field. Use the sample instead of an important document.
steps: Select text in the practice field. Use the sample instead of an important document.
Press Command + X.
The selection is removed and can be pasted elsewhere.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The selection is removed and can be pasted elsewhere.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Select all text
shortcuts.summary: Select all text in the current text field.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the practice field to give it keyboard focus.
steps: Click in the practice field to give it keyboard focus.
Press Command + A.
All text in the field is highlighted.
shortcuts.expectedResult: All text in the field is highlighted.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Undo an edit
shortcuts.summary: Reverse the most recent undoable text edit.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Type a few characters or delete some text in the practice field.
steps: Type a few characters or delete some text in the practice field.
Press Command + Z.
The last edit is undone and the previous text is restored.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The last edit is undone and the previous text is restored.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Redo an edit
shortcuts.summary: Repeat the edit you just undid.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Edit the practice text, then press Command + Z once.
steps: Edit the practice text, then press Command + Z once.
Press Shift + Command + Z.
The undone edit is applied again.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The undone edit is applied again.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Go to document beginning
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor to the beginning of the document.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the middle of the practice text so the cursor is visible.
steps: Click in the middle of the practice text so the cursor is visible.
Press Command + Up Arrow.
The cursor moves to the very beginning of the text.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the very beginning of the text.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Go to document end
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor to the end of the document.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the first half of the practice text.
steps: Click in the first half of the practice text.
Press Command + Down Arrow.
The cursor moves to the end of the text.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the end of the text.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Go to line beginning
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor to the beginning of the current visual line.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
steps: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
Press Command + Left Arrow.
The cursor moves to the beginning of the line.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the beginning of the line.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Go to line end
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor to the end of the current visual line.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
steps: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
Press Command + Right Arrow.
The cursor moves to the end of the line.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the end of the line.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Move backward one word
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor backward by a word instead of a character.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click just after a word in the English sample text.
steps: Click just after a word in the English sample text.
Press Option + Left Arrow.
The cursor moves to the beginning of the previous word.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the beginning of the previous word.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.
Word movement can differ between Chinese text and space-separated English. Try the English sample first.

shortcuts.title: Move forward one word
shortcuts.summary: Move the cursor forward by a word instead of a character.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click just before a word in the English sample text.
steps: Click just before a word in the English sample text.
Press Option + Right Arrow.
The cursor moves to the end of the next word.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The cursor moves to the end of the next word.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.
Word movement can differ between Chinese text and space-separated English. Try the English sample first.

shortcuts.title: Delete the previous word
shortcuts.summary: Delete the word or word segment before the cursor.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click just after a word in the English practice sentence.
steps: Click just after a word in the English practice sentence.
Press Option + Delete.
Text before the cursor is deleted. Press Command + Z to restore it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Text before the cursor is deleted. Press Command + Z to restore it.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.
Word movement can differ between Chinese text and space-separated English. Try the English sample first.

shortcuts.title: Delete the next character
shortcuts.summary: Delete the character after the cursor.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Place the cursor between two characters in the practice text.
steps: Place the cursor between two characters in the practice text.
Press Fn + Delete.
The next character is deleted. Press Command + Z to restore it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The next character is deleted. Press Command + Z to restore it.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Select to end of line
shortcuts.summary: Select text from the cursor to the end of the current line.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
steps: Click in the middle of a line in the practice text.
Press Shift + Command + Right Arrow.
Text from the cursor to the end of the line is highlighted.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Text from the cursor to the end of the line is highlighted.
notes: This action applies inside a text field. It behaves differently when focus is in a folder, list, or another app.

shortcuts.title: Find in a document
shortcuts.summary: Open Find in the current app or document.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Bring a document that supports Find to the front.
steps: Bring a document that supports Find to the front.
Press Command + F.
A Find bar or panel appears for entering a search term.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A Find bar or panel appears for entering a search term.
notes: Find is provided by the current app. A browser searches the page, while Finder searches files.

shortcuts.title: Find next match
shortcuts.summary: Go to the next occurrence of the search term.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Search for a repeated word in a document that supports Find.
steps: Search for a repeated word in a document that supports Find.
Press Command + G.
The next match is selected or scrolled into view.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The next match is selected or scrolled into view.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Find previous match
shortcuts.summary: Go to the previous occurrence of the search term.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Search for a repeated word in a document that supports Find.
steps: Search for a repeated word in a document that supports Find.
Press Shift + Command + G.
The previous match is selected or scrolled into view.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The previous match is selected or scrolled into view.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Minimize a window
shortcuts.summary: Minimize the practice window to the Dock.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Open the separate practice window and bring it to the front.
steps: Open the separate practice window and bring it to the front.
Press Command + M.
The window minimizes to the Dock. Click its thumbnail to restore it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The window minimizes to the Dock. Click its thumbnail to restore it.
notes: The main reference window stays open. Restore the practice window from its Dock thumbnail or an available restore control.

shortcuts.title: Close a window
shortcuts.summary: Close the current window or tab.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Use the separate practice window and save any other documents first.
steps: Use the separate practice window and save any other documents first.
Press Command + W.
The practice window closes; the main reference window remains open.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The practice window closes; the main reference window remains open.
notes: Closing a window does not quit the app. Apps with tabs usually close the active tab first.

shortcuts.title: Hide the current app
shortcuts.summary: Temporarily hide all windows of the current app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Remember how to return: click QuickKey in the Dock.
steps: Remember how to return: click QuickKey in the Dock.
Press Command + H.
The app's windows hide and reappear when you click its Dock icon.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The app's windows hide and reappear when you click its Dock icon.
notes: A hidden app keeps running. Click its icon in the Dock to return.

shortcuts.title: Hide other apps
shortcuts.summary: Keep the current app visible and hide other apps.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Open two apps and bring the one you want to keep visible to the front.
steps: Open two apps and bring the one you want to keep visible to the front.
Press Option + Command + H.
Other apps' windows hide while the current app stays visible.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Other apps' windows hide while the current app stays visible.
notes: Click another app's Dock icon to show its windows again.

shortcuts.title: Quit the current app
shortcuts.summary: Stop the current app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Save your documents in the target app. Avoid quitting QuickKey during practice.
steps: Save your documents in the target app. Avoid quitting QuickKey during practice.
Press Command + Q.
The target app quits. Reopen it from the Dock or Spotlight.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The target app quits. Reopen it from the Dock or Spotlight.
notes: This quits the app rather than just closing a window. Do not practice on important unsaved documents.

shortcuts.title: Open Force Quit
shortcuts.summary: View running apps and handle an unresponsive app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Inspect the panel without actually force-quitting an app.
steps: Inspect the panel without actually force-quitting an app.
Press Option + Command + Escape.
The Force Quit Applications panel appears. Press Esc to close it.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The Force Quit Applications panel appears. Press Esc to close it.
notes: Force Quit can lose unsaved changes. To learn the shortcut, open the panel and cancel.

shortcuts.title: Save a document
shortcuts.summary: Write changes in the current document to disk.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Create a test document and bring its app to the front.
steps: Create a test document and bring its app to the front.
Press Command + S.
The document is saved. Its first save may ask for a name and location.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The document is saved. Its first save may ask for a name and location.
notes: If the expected result does not appear, check the active app and keyboard focus, then inspect the shortcut shown in its menu bar.

shortcuts.title: Open the Print dialog
shortcuts.summary: Inspect printing options for the current document.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Open a printable test document. You do not need a printer for practice.
steps: Open a printable test document. You do not need a printer for practice.
Press Command + P.
The Print dialog appears. Cancel or press Esc to return without printing.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The Print dialog appears. Cancel or press Esc to return without printing.
notes: The shortcut only opens print settings. You can cancel without sending a print job.

shortcuts.title: Bold text
shortcuts.summary: Toggle bold formatting for the selected text.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Select some text in the native practice field below.
steps: Select some text in the native practice field below.
Press Command + B.
The selection becomes bold, or returns to regular weight if it was already bold.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The selection becomes bold, or returns to regular weight if it was already bold.
notes: Select text in the practice field. Feedback checks actual changes to font or underline attributes.

shortcuts.title: Italicize text
shortcuts.summary: Toggle italic formatting for the selected text.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Select some text in the native practice field below.
steps: Select some text in the native practice field below.
Press Command + I.
The selection becomes italic, or existing italic formatting is removed.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The selection becomes italic, or existing italic formatting is removed.
notes: Select text in the practice field. Feedback checks actual changes to font or underline attributes.
Some fonts have no italic face, so the visual change may be subtle. Try a font that supports italics.

shortcuts.title: Underline text
shortcuts.summary: Toggle underlining for the selected text.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Select some text in the native practice field below.
steps: Select some text in the native practice field below.
Press Command + U.
The selection is underlined, or existing underlining is removed.
shortcuts.expectedResult: The selection is underlined, or existing underlining is removed.
notes: Select text in the practice field. Feedback checks actual changes to font or underline attributes.

shortcuts.title: F1 · Decrease brightness
shortcuts.summary: Lower brightness on a display that supports keyboard controls.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
steps: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
Press F1 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
Display brightness decreases or the brightness indicator appears.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Display brightness decreases or the brightness indicator appears.
notes: Some external displays do not support this key. Use the display's own controls when needed.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F2 · Increase brightness
shortcuts.summary: Raise brightness on a display that supports keyboard controls.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
steps: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
Press F2 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
Display brightness increases or the brightness indicator appears.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Display brightness increases or the brightness indicator appears.
notes: Brightness cannot increase past its maximum. Some external displays do not support this key.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F3 · Mission Control
shortcuts.summary: View open windows and desktop spaces.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
steps: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
Press F3 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
Mission Control appears. Press Esc or the same function key to return.
shortcuts.expectedResult: Mission Control appears. Press Esc or the same function key to return.
notes: Change the Mission Control binding in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F4 · Search or Launchpad
shortcuts.summary: The magnifying-glass key on newer keyboards usually opens Spotlight.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
steps: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
Press F4 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
A magnifying-glass key opens search; an older grid-icon key may open Launchpad.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A magnifying-glass key opens search; an older grid-icon key may open Launchpad.
notes: F4 on newer Apple keyboards often opens Spotlight; older F4 keys may open Launchpad. Follow the keycap icon.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F5 · Dictation or backlight
shortcuts.summary: A microphone key usually starts Dictation; an older backlight key may dim keyboard lighting.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Place the cursor in editable text. Whether the microphone key needs Fn depends on your function-key settings.
steps: Place the cursor in editable text. Whether the microphone key needs Fn depends on your function-key settings.
Press F5 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
A microphone key may open Dictation; an older backlight key may dim the keyboard.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A microphone key may open Dictation; an older backlight key may dim the keyboard.
notes: Enable Dictation and place the cursor in editable text first. F5 on some older keyboards dims keyboard lighting. Holding the microphone key may behave differently with Siri and model settings.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F6 · Do Not Disturb or backlight
shortcuts.summary: A moon key usually controls Do Not Disturb; an older backlight key may brighten keyboard lighting.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
steps: Follow your keycap icon and Fn settings. With standard function keys enabled, media functions usually need Fn.
Press F6 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
A moon key toggles Do Not Disturb; an older backlight key may brighten the keyboard.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A moon key toggles Do Not Disturb; an older backlight key may brighten the keyboard.
notes: F6 on some older keyboards brightens keyboard lighting. Check the keycap instead of assuming it always enables Do Not Disturb.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F7 · Previous or rewind
shortcuts.summary: Control the previous item or rewind in the current media app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Prepare playable media. Whether media keys need Fn depends on your function-key settings.
steps: Prepare playable media. Whether media keys need Fn depends on your function-key settings.
Press F7 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
A supported player goes to the previous item or rewinds; behavior depends on the player.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A supported player goes to the previous item or rewinds; behavior depends on the player.
notes: Open controllable audio, video, or a slideshow first. With no active player, this key may produce no visible response.
System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys lets you toggle “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys.”
This page describes common top-row functions on Apple keyboards. Standard F-key behavior is set by the current app or custom bindings.
On Touch Bar Macs, hold Fn to show F1–F12. Third-party keyboards may use different icons or Fn-lock behavior.

shortcuts.title: F8 · Play or pause
shortcuts.summary: Toggle playback in the current media app.
shortcuts.prerequisite: Prepare playable media. Whether media keys need Fn depends on your function-key settings.
steps: Prepare playable media. Whether media keys need Fn depends on your function-key settings.
Press F8 with Fn if your function-key settings require it.
A supported player starts or pauses playback.
shortcuts.expectedResult: A supported player starts or pauses playback.
notes: Controllable media must be available. The system and player determine which media target receives the key.
